note: Fits the profile on everything except money and need. Successful: self-employed, runs his own expedition adventure race as event director, physics degree, published a book on endurance training — a business owner in the sense the ICP means. Good to great: about as pure a case as the corpus contains, in his own words 'there's nothing wrong right now' and he is 'looking to optimize'. Not deconditioned: 12% body fat at 50, climbing three or four nights a week, training eight to ten sessions a week — the opposite of the excluded profile, and the rep said so out loud, 'you're not our typical client because you're way ahead.' Misses income: a $4,000 fee is 'a substantial portion of my annual income', becomes roughly NZ$7,500 after exchange, and only works if his accountant lets him expense it — this is the same failure mode as the Badrane Hriouch assessment, a good profile with no willingness or capacity to pay. Misses neglected_health: the criterion assumes health is the neglected area, and his health is the least neglected thing in his life; what he actually lacks is kettlebell technical knowledge, which is a narrower and cheaper want than the programme is priced for. Judged on the criteria, not the outcome — the call ended in a follow-up, and the edge rating reflects the income and need gaps that were visible well before price was quoted.
